edits.before: Configuration choices affect the runtime and resource allocation of batch data-processing jobs. SAFE-Pipe implements a bounded advisor that compares eight local Dask configurations using workload metadata, a fitted runtime predictor, a calibrated upper runtime estimate and explicit support checks. The original study measured four fixed synthetic workload profiles across eight configurations with three repetitions, producing 96 successful runs on one Windows PC. A grouped held-out evaluation reported median absolute percentage error of 13.84%, compared with 23.01% for a family-median baseline, on 24 test rows belonging to eight family/configuration groups. A historical resource-cost comparison reused the original table and is therefore descriptive rather than independent evidence of savings. Subsequent research examined whether small execution probes preserve memory-pressure information from full jobs. Stage A recorded 41 successful full attempts and seven execution errors; all 96 Stage B probes completed quietly, although eight of 32 paired comparison groups disagreed with full-input pressure. A one-probe development replay added profiling cost without changing the stronger metadata-based choices. Probe admission consequently remains disabled. The latest original-advisor implementation passed 143 Windows software tests, while fresh prospective validation remains pending. The contribution is an auditable, scope-limited advisor and an evidence-based investigation of profiling limits, not a universal safety guarantee or a validated failure classifier.
